purpose: Operating-price benchmark for the three RTS-GMLC areas: Arizona (Phoenix), Nevada (Las Vegas), California (Los Angeles). Used to contrast the electricity-price gap against the PUE/heat-sink advantage when evaluating cross-site workload migration.

sources.publisher: U.S. Energy Information Administration, state electricity data (annual, through 2020)

conventions.price: average retail price, cents/kWh, 'Total Electric Industry' rows

caveats: EIA state averages blend all utilities in the state; Los Angeles load is served by LADWP plus SCE, and APS/NV Energy tariffs differ from the state average.
These files end at 2020, which matches the 2020 load and weather series but must not be extrapolated as current prices without a newer vintage.
State average prices include transmission and distribution charges; a large load's marginal price also depends on its voltage class and contract.
